sections:
## Reconciliation Notes

- **Depth:** rigorous (lane `rigorous` from `lane.mjs --range`: 3 810 lines, 102 files, the session and ipc sensitive words, a manifest change). Security ran on every shard; the interaction sweep and the gap-finder ran.
- **Scope:** `fdda65e..d7a0e22` resolved as an explicit range (base `cb84fe8`, so the docs-only commit `fdda65e` is included; it adds no code). 102 reviewable files, 928 generated/evidence files excluded. Final code `aabd716`; later commits are docs.
- **Read-only, nothing heavy (coordinator constraint):** typecheck, knip, jscpd and dependency-cruiser were not re-run; slice evidence records them green on the final code. Biome lint (0), ast-grep smells (1 empty catch, accepted S6-M7), ast-grep and opengrep sinks (0 in changed files) and rg risk keywords (0) ran.
- **CodeScene `analyze_change_set` (base `fdda65e`):** the quality gate fails only on three `.rpiv/artifacts/evidence/**` measurement scripts (outside the reviewable scope, knip-ignored). Product files are stable; `project-registration-flow.ts` improved. No product Code Health finding.
- **Orchestration deviations:** the Discovery Map was passed to Wave-2 by file path, not pasted; the 588 KB source shard and the 594 KB test shard each got two Quality agents (desktop and harness file subsets); the five small config/docs shards shared one Quality and one Security agent. Wave-2 isolation held: no raw Wave-1 output reached a lens. Dependencies and CVE lenses were not dispatched: the manifest change adds a script only (no dependency added, bumped or removed). Predicate-trace (4a) skipped: no mismatched predicate rows.
- **Accepted residuals not re-raised** (from the brief and decisions §131-§139): Z4 and the non-Error "ManagedRuntime disposed" rejection (lens rows on harness-runtime-shutdown.test.ts:504 and :551), W4 canary 2 of 8 rules (tsconfig.base.json:32), the gate-script mutants and their test gaps (#139: stryker.project-storage.config.json:50, check-effect-diagnostics.test.mjs:333 and :405), Z6 test-only observer close facade (project-registration-observer.ts:85). Six lens rows dropped this way.
- **Compound kept on accepted residuals:** I1 combines the accepted W12 and W13 with the unchanged shutdown sink and Q33; that is why it stays, at 🟡 after the verifier's Weakened.
- **Verification:** 57 findings verified; 38 Verified, 18 Weakened (each demoted one tier), 1 Falsified (Q54, withdrawn). The InScopeFiles pre-filter dropped 0 findings (InScopeFiles = ChangedFiles).
- **Precedent weighting:** `process-bootstrap.ts` has two precedents with 30-day follow-ups (`615df7a`, `daee118`); Q26 and Q27 carry `[precedent-weighted]` (both then Weakened).
- **Peer mirror:** 19 stem-heuristic pairs, nearly all unrelated file kinds; no actionable Missing/Diverged row, no bump.
- **Cascade detection:** no stranded-state, duplicate-processing or contradictory-predicate triple fired. IX-1 (masking) became I1; IX-2 (false-promise, Low) folded into Q20 and G3; IX-3 (contradictory design, Low) folded into Q30.

## Pattern Analysis

The peer comparator ran on 19 pairs chosen by file-name stem. They pair unlike kinds (mutation configs with tsconfig files, the desktop request core with the harness runtime, a producer with its consumer), so 166 rows are Intentionally-absent and 8 Mirrored. The only content-level difference worth naming is that the desktop core drops the `retryable` flag of `request.failure`; the bridges do not use it today. No peer finding.

## Impact

- `apps/harness/src/storage/project-storage-node-errors.ts` has 14 production consumers (the one storage-failure guard, s2).
- `apps/harness/src/storage/permit-lock.ts` serves the coordinator, the canonical writer, the registration flow and the locks facade (s1).
- `apps/harness/src/registration/registry-database.ts` has 20 consumers; the standalone-authority ownership (s4) reaches all of them.
- `apps/desktop/src/main/harness-request-core.ts` now sits under all three bridges and two failure mappers (s7).
- Renderer → main IPC handlers keep `decodeStrict` on every input and gain the shutdown gate; no sender-frame check (pre-existing, window-level lockdown only).

## Precedents

| hash | subject | 30d-follow-ups | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `887804d` | drain the Project Storage owner through Effect | 1 (`f4e83c8`, same day) | a completion registered before the operation started hung stop on a synchronous throw |
| `615df7a` | owners from Layers, Effect-owned shutdown | 2 (`7058508`, `43bc303`) | shutdown re-entry and same-turn ordering broke once |
| `00f4a23` / `ff162f5` | Effect permit lock; #110 split | in-slice | fair hand-off regressed once; packaged load order |
| `f810132` | desktop supervisor timing and shutdown through Effect | 2 (`c417342`, `43bc303`) | settlement timing is a tested contract |
| `8a0658d`, `fb8e1d9` | isolate correlated request failures; define requests once | 0 | per-request isolation must hold across bridges |
| `daee118` | application.db authority | 5 (`18d9761`, `32c52fa`, `b1e32cb`, `667bc44`, `9aab1cc`) | lazy creation, joining in-flight creation, stop last |
| `d91833f` | Effect tsgo language service | 2 (`e7f1ba1`, `0ff211e`) | tooling additions get late config and docs follow-ups |

Composite lessons: ordering keeps breaking (each slice pinned its order with bindings, and mutation closed each slice); synchronous throws inside drains hang shutdown (not reproduced here); Promise facades hide fail versus die (the range needed kill rounds for s5 to s8 and the combined run); tooling additions need docs and config follow-ups (Q9, Q13, Q16).

## Spec Conformance

checked #123 "Effect migration remainder: dedicated pass for existing SQL bodies and the Unit 2 lifecycle (one ManagedRuntime per process)" — 3 met · 3 partial · 4 missing · 1 contradicted · 12 extra

- Met: one ManagedRuntime per harness process (`apps/harness/src/process-bootstrap.ts:135`), services at ownership boundaries, explicit shutdown sequencing.
- Partial: a design exists but no plan file; replaced coordination removed (`harness-pending-request.ts` deleted, listing stop chain in Effect) but D4 facades kept and a hand-written fair lock added (decided D2, D4).
- Missing (Part B by recorded decision §102-§103; no SQL body changed): the SQL-body pass, its before/after performance, the viability analysis, new SQL in Effect.
- Contradicted: "behaviour unchanged" — Part A deliberately changes FIFO order, close deadlines and the stdout drain.
- Extra: the desktop ManagedRuntime, the shared bridge core, the #96 drain, the `check:effect` gate and waiver register, the storage-failure guard, the deadlines and budgets, the mutation configs.

rpiv contract conformance: run /rpiv:validate .rpiv/artifacts/designs/2026-10-17_00-35-29_effect-unit2b-runtime-lifecycle-part-a.md

## Recommendation

**Verdict: no critical defect. Three important findings, all documentary or observability, none a wrong result, lost data or security exposure.** Part A composes: one ManagedRuntime per process (harness `process-bootstrap.ts:135`, desktop `desktop-runtime.ts:202`), acquireRelease and Layers for owners, the fair lock on Deferred, typed unconfirmed outcomes, no app-to-app import, one storage-failure guard (shared-vocab-union) and no new unregistered `new Promise`.

| ID | Root mechanism | Choice for Pedro |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I1 | the harness process edge has no slot for the failure value, so every typed diagnostic Part A adds is lost (broken is still never reported clean) | (a) one small follow-up slice to log a redacted summary and split the startup code; (b) accept as a residual alongside W12/W13 |
| Q33 | the 3 s shutdown budget runs the listing parts in sequence, so an owner close that outruns it leaves Git inspections unaborted | (a) start the observer abort independently; (b) accept as residual (the process exits right after) |
| Q25 | process-entry.ts is TDD-exempt by the brief, so the new startup ordering has no test | (a) extract and pin it; (b) keep the exemption and name it in the acceptance record |

The 🔵 items group into four mechanisms: stale s6 mutation ranges and unwired per-slice configs (Q1-Q9, Q13, Q14); test-quality polish (Q39-Q42, Q50, Q51, Q57, Q58); small bridge consistency gaps (Q17-Q19, Q21-Q23, G3); and harness tidy-ups (Q24, Q26-Q29, Q31, Q34-Q38, G2). None blocks on its own.

findings.title: Part A's typed shutdown and startup diagnostics are all discarded at the harness process edge

quoted: failStartup("Harness received an invalid bootstrap message.");

findings.why: Part A builds distinct typed failures (RegistrationCleanupUnconfirmed with named parts, ApplicationDatabaseCloseUnconfirmed, HarnessRuntimeDisposeUnconfirmed, ordered AggregateErrors), but both edges keep only a code and a fixed text: apps/harness/src/process-shutdown.ts:19 calls failed("Harness shutdown failed.") without the value, and the startup catch logs every start or dispose failure as an invalid bootstrap message. Constituents Q24, Q26, Q27, Q33, Q34. A broken stop or start is never reported as clean (fatal code plus exit 1), so the core of degrade-distinguishes-broken holds; what is lost is every distinct diagnostic the slices added, and the field cannot tell a lost authority close from an unconfirmed listing cleanup.
findings.fix: Pass the failure value to the two fatal sinks and log a redacted summary (the failure _tag values and RegistrationCleanupUnconfirmed parts, never paths or messages), and give the startup catch a separate code for a runtime start or dispose failure versus an invalid bootstrap message. One small slice; the residuals W12 and W13 then shrink to the bound only.
findings.verifyNote: Narrower than critical: process-shutdown.ts and the fixed-text fatal logging are unchanged since fdda65e; Layer and start failures already reached this catch at the base; Part A adds the bounded-dispose failures and the typed shutdown aggregate; broken is never reported clean (process-entry.ts:33-34, :38-39); the startup side is recorded as residual W12 (brief :2842). Kept as a compound because the accepted residuals W12 and W13 combine with the unchanged shutdown sink and Q33 so that no Part A diagnostic is ever observable.

quoted: async function connect(port: UtilityMessagePort, bootstrap: unknown): Promise<void> {

findings.title: When the owner close outruns the 3 s shutdown budget, the observer's active Git inspections are never aborted
findings.why: The owner close drains preparations under its own 5 000 ms budget (apps/harness/src/registration/project-registration-preparation.ts:274-278), longer than REGISTRATION_SHUTDOWN_CLEANUP_BUDGET_MS = 3 000. The chain timeout then interrupts at :53, before observer.closeEffect (:54) starts, so apps/harness/src/project-registration-observer.ts:150 never aborts the running inspections, and the owner's distinct pendingCreation, pendingListing and pendingCleanup outcomes are folded into a bare 'listing' part. The brief pins the sequential order on purpose (brief :891), but not this consequence.
findings.fix: Start the observer close (or at least its abort signal) independently of the owner close, for example Effect.all over the three parts with explicit concurrency inside the one budget, or abort inspections first; keep the named parts from whatever finished.

findings.title: AGENTS.md does not document the waiver register rules the Effect gate blocks on

quoted: - Type checking authority: `pnpm typecheck` (the project's TypeScript, currently 6.0.2) is the type-checking authority. The editor and agent LSP is Effect tsgo (TypeScript-Go 7 plus the Effect language service, enabled by the `@effect/language-service` plugin in `tsconfig.base.json`). In the editor, an error that only the LSP reports is advisory: investigate it. `pnpm check:effect`, which runs inside `pnpm check`, runs the same Effect build in tsc mode and blocks on every error it reports: each `error`-level Effect diagnostic, and any other error, including a type error that only TypeScript-Go reports, which the gate reports as a broken run and never as clean. Effect `warning` diagnostics stay advice unless a reviewer and the user promote one to a rule.

findings.fix: Add one sentence: a suppression needs a `// Effect waiver EW<n>: <reason>.` line above the directive and a matching entry in apps/harness/scripts/effect-diagnostics-waivers.json.
